scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The twist traces its stylistic lineage to African-American and African traditions, with historians Marshall and Jean Stearns noting that a pelvic dance motion called the twist came to America from the Congo during slavery.
Early iterations appeared in blackface minstrelsy with Joel Walker Sweeney's 'Vine Twist' and the early 20th-century craze 'Mess Around'.
Blues artists referenced the concept decades prior to the 1950s boom, including Bo Carter's 'Twist It Babe' in 1931 and Jelly Roll Morton's 'Winin' Boy Blues'.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The twist is performed standing with feet approximately shoulder-width apart.
The hips, torso, and legs rotate on the balls of the feet as a single unit, with feet grinding back and forth on the floor as if putting out a cigarette.
Knees are bent slightly, and arms are held out from the body, bent at the elbow.
Watch for Cigarette Stomp, Towel Wipe.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Chubby Checker, Hank Ballard, Dick Clark, Joey Dee, Bill Haley, Sam Cooke, Bo Diddley.

Exported internationally, yielding localized versions such as Mexico's 'Spanish Twist' and 'Florida Twist' by Bill Haley, French yé-yé adaptations by Johnny Hallyday and Eddy Mitchell, and British pop versions.
Influenced subsequent 1960s fad dances including the Jerk, the Pony, the Watusi, the Mashed Potato, the Monkey, and the Funky Chicken.

Twist is variant of Pony: A novelty dance spawned during the twist era.
Twist is variant of Watusi: Follow-up solo dance craze of the early 1960s.
Twist is variant of Mashed Potato: Popular 1960s dance sharing structural lineage with the twist.
